page: Amazon Web Services c7i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at 3.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). It is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in compute-heavy workloads. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core and multi-core Geekbench evaluations, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark CPU tests, including physics and encryption. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached speeds reaching 3865.15 GB/sec and uncached speeds at 203.15 GB/sec. However, write speeds for large blocks and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the average performance tier.

This instance is designed for compute-intensive tasks, including static web serving, database operations, and small-to-medium LLM inference, where it demonstrates strong prompt processing and text generation capabilities. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound applications that do not require massive memory footprints, though it is less suitable for large-scale memory-resident databases or heavy GPU-accelerated tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 96.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The processor supports advanced instruction sets like Intel AMX and AVX-512. While it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, it delivers strong benchmark performance in software compilation, cryptography, and database operations, alongside high read-only memory bandwidth. This configuration is highly suited for compute-bound workloads, static web serving, and small-to-medium language model inference, offering a balanced resource profile for applications that prioritize raw CPU throughput over massive memory capacity or local disk I/O.
